newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - June 19.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - June 19.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following business stories Thursday:
* Technology stocks took a hit after Seagate Technology Inc and Gateway 2000 Inc offered grim earnings forecasts and after Intel Corp said it planned to cut prices on its Pentium computer chips.
* A Federal Reserve survey known as the beige book shows "pockets of weakness" in the 12 districts it monitors.
* British Aerospace Plc has joined Lockheed Martin in its bid for the multibillion-dollar U.S. joint strike fighter program.
* Westinghouse has changed its plans to separate its media and industrial businesses and has decided that the Thermo King refrigerated transport group will remain part of its media division.
* Market Place: Gold prices are defying expectations, dropping 6.8 percent this year while the world economy is set to grow at its fastest pace in nearly a decade and currency markets are uncertain.

* Walt Disney Co, long the epitome of American family values, is under fire from Southern Baptists, who have launched a boycott over concerns about the company's policies toward gays and some of the movies Disney has churned out recently.
* Lehman Brothers is selling One Times Square for about $110 million, ringing up a hefty profit from the $27.5 million it doled out for the property two years ago, sources said.
* South African mining company Gencor Ltd is spinning of its base metals, minerals and coal units and is acquiring Australian nickel producer, QNI Ltd.
* Robert Elliott, a partner at KPMG Peat Marwick LLP, appears to be the leading contender to be the next chairman of the Financial Accounting Standards Board.
* Steven Jobs has filed to sell all but 1 of the 1.5 million shares of Apple Computer Inc that he purchased when he sold Next Software to Apple.
* Fidelity Investments, the largest mutual fund company in the United States, plans to lay off 200 to 250 employees.

* The Securities and Exchange Commission has obtained an order against a British Virgin Islands mutual fund in an attempt to clarify a rule on selling stock overseas without registering it in the United States.
* Airlines are becoming increasingly aggressive in ensuring they depart on time, leaving tardy passengers behind in order to stay on schedule.
* Goldman Sachs & Co posted a record $1.52 billion in earnings in the first half of its fiscal year, a 19 percent increase from the same period in the prior year.
* Barney's Inc, the luxury clothier now in bankruptcy, has a potential suitor: the investment firm of Texas Pacific Group.
* Federal Communications Commission Chairman Reed Hundt is expected to criticize a possible merger between AT&T Corp with regional Bell SBC Communications.
